summary: This is a Docker Compose configuration that sets up two services: an app built from the current directory that exposes port 8000, and a belgif-lint service that validates OpenAPI specifications using Maven. The belgif-lint service reuses a Maven cache volume across runs to speed up builds.

explanations.5: The double-percent syntax (%%port=8000%%) is a template variable that gets replaced at runtime; it maps port 8000 on your machine to port 80 inside the container.
explanations.7: This mounts the main.py file from your computer into the container at /code/main.py, so changes you make locally are immediately visible inside the running container.
explanations.11: This pulls a pre-built Docker image that has Maven 3.9.9 and Java 17 already installed, rather than building from scratch.
explanations.13: The 'ro' flag means read-only—the container can see these files but can't modify them, which prevents accidental changes to your source code.
explanations.14: This creates a persistent volume that stores Maven dependencies between container runs, so Maven doesn't re-download everything each time.
explanations.16: The '>' character allows the long command to be split across multiple lines for readability; Docker concatenates them back together.
